papers.title: Processing speed, not multitasking, drives expert decision-making under pressure.
papers.reason: The title suggests a human behavioural study of decision-making under pressure and multitasking, relevant to executive performance but not clearly a computational model or clinical assessment paper.

papers.title: Motor cortex-based intracortical BCI performance is robust to changes in attentional load during dual-tasking.
papers.reason: This human study manipulates attentional and working-memory load with an N-back dual task while measuring EEG correlates, making it relevant to executive attention despite its primary BCI focus.

papers.title: Prefrontal circuitry abnormalities and cognitive impairment in adolescents with early-onset psychosis.
papers.reason: The paper appears to address prefrontal neural abnormalities and cognitive impairment in a clinical human population, plausibly relevant to executive dysfunction but not clearly focused on planning, working memory, or attention from the available text.

papers.title: Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (tDCS) and Smoking Cessation: Clinical and Neurocognitive Outcomes Among Turkish Adults.
papers.reason: This appears to concern clinical and neurocognitive outcomes of tDCS for smoking cessation, with no clear connection to executive-function modelling or cognitive impairment assessment in the provided information.

papers.title: Nogo-related frontal theta-band activity after magnetic seizure therapy in treatment-resistant depression: an exploratory task-based EEG study
papers.reason: This task-based EEG study directly examines frontal midline theta during Go/Nogo response inhibition in depression, although the findings are exploratory and not robust after correction.

papers.title: Default mode network connectivity and temperament are associated with internalizing symptoms in early childhood.
papers.reason: The study links resting-state connectivity and temperament to internalizing symptoms in children, with only indirect relevance to executive function through frontoparietal cognitive-control network measures.

papers.title: Can neuroimaging unlock precision therapeutics in psychosis spectrum disorders?
papers.reason: The title suggests a broad neuroimaging and treatment-focused psychosis review rather than executive-function modelling, cognitive-control neuroscience, or digital cognitive assessment.

papers.title: Impaired brain reserve is associated with increased risk of overt hepatic encephalopathy occurrence in patients with cirrhosis
papers.reason: The paper concerns human brain reserve and encephalopathy risk, which is broadly relevant to cognitive impairment but not specifically centred on planning, working memory, attention, or cognitive-control modelling.

papers.title: Multimodal Detection of Cognitive Impairment in Non-Neurological Rehabilitation Settings: The COGinREHAB Study Protocol
papers.reason: This is a multimodal clinical cognitive-impairment detection protocol combining cognitive screening, neuropsychological assessment, plasma biomarkers, EEG vigilance, P300, actigraphy, and polysomnography.

papers.title: Sturge – Weber Syndrome in Children: Clinical Course Features Based on Two Case Reports
papers.reason: The case reports include EEG, MRI, and cognitive-developmental outcomes, but the focus is epilepsy and clinical heterogeneity rather than executive function or cognitive assessment methodology.

papers.title: Functional brain activity in cancer-related cognitive impairment: a scoping review of EEG studies.
papers.reason: The review maps EEG paradigms and cognitive outcomes in cancer-related cognitive impairment, including P300 and attention tasks, making it relevant to clinical cognitive biomarkers though not specifically executive-function modelling.
